chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ali ibn Muhammad said:

I asked him: Do we take from the rulings of the opponents what they take from us in their rulings? He wrote to me, peace be upon him: 'It is permissible for you to do so, if God wills, if your approach in it is precaution (taqiyyah) from them and accommodation to them.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: precaution or prudence in religious practice to avoid harm
key_terms.الْمُخَالِفِينَ: the opponents (referring to other Islamic sects or schools)
key_terms.الْمُدَارَاة: accommodation or gentle handling in social/legal dealings

ai.seo_question: Can Shia Muslims apply the same legal rulings to non-Shia Muslims that those non-Shia apply to them?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the principle of *ta'abbud* (legal reciprocity), allowing Shias to adopt the juristic rulings of their opponents against them, a practice rooted in the strategic necessity of *taqiyyah* (precaution) and *mudarāh* (accommodation). This ruling is particularly significant in contexts of political or social minority status, where aligning with the dominant school of thought protects the community from persecution or legal disadvantage. It reflects the pragmatic flexibility of Shia fiqh in navigating inter-sectarian relations while maintaining theological distinctiveness.
